cards.explanation: The answer is False. God says it straight to Ezekiel: "But you must not mourn or weep or let your tears flow." (Ezekiel 24:16) So no weeping and no tears for him. This is one of the heavy parts of the passage, friends. I think this one hurts.

The answer is his turban and his sandals. God says, "Put on your turban and strap your sandals on your feet…" (Ezekiel 24:17) A turban is a head wrap. The turban goes on his head, and the sandals go on his feet, friends. Those are the two things God names.

The answer is False. God tells Ezekiel, "do not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners." (Ezekiel 24:17) The bread of mourners is off the table for him, friends. I think that's a hard word to carry.

The answer is wife. Ezekiel says, "So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died." (Ezekiel 24:18) Morning to evening, and everything changed, friends. I think this is one of the heaviest lines in the whole book.

The answer is what his actions mean for them. The people ask, "Won’t you tell us what these things you are doing mean to us?" (Ezekiel 24:19) They see a man who isn't mourning, and they want to know what it has to do with them, friends. Ezekiel's actions are doing the talking before he says a word.

The answer is God's own sanctuary. God says, "I am about to desecrate My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and the delight of your soul." (Ezekiel 24:21) Notice, friends, He calls it "My sanctuary." It's His, and He calls it the desire of their eyes.
The answer is True. God says, "And the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword." (Ezekiel 24:21) This is a heavy line, friends. I think it's okay to sit with that for a second.
The answer is False. Ezekiel says, "Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet." (Ezekiel 24:23) They stay on, friends. The people will do just what Ezekiel did.

The answer is sins. Ezekiel says, "You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your sins, and you will groan among yourselves." (Ezekiel 24:23) The text gives the reason right there, friends. It's a sober line, and I'll let it stand as it is.

The answer is that He is the Lord GOD. God says, "Thus Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do everything that he has done. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 24:24) A sign points to something, friends. Here it points to who God is.

The answer is that he will speak and no longer be mute. God says, "On that day your mouth will be opened to him who has escaped; you will speak and no longer be mute." (Ezekiel 24:27) The one who escaped brings the news, and Ezekiel's mouth is opened, friends. Ezekiel will be a sign to them, just like God said.
